question: Can an independent modern astronomical absolute-time anchor discriminate Ming Datong qishuo geography, and what uncertainty/semantic layers must be closed before such a comparison is historically admissible?

modern_ephemeris.historical_lunar_use: DE431 is explicitly designed as the long integration more suitable for times more than a few centuries in the past than DE430.

solar_time_semantics.equation_of_time_definition: apparent solar time - mean solar time
solar_time_semantics.key_distinction: The ~16-minute value is not an ephemeris uncertainty; it is a deterministic coordinate-semantic difference if one compares apparent versus mean solar time.

existing_source_constraint.source: Batch 11G / Zhou Xiang 1569 推合朔時刻法
existing_source_constraint.consequence: ZI_ZHENG labels define the internal clock origin but do not by themselves prove local apparent solar midnight at a named longitude.

required_before_numeric_meridian_adjudic: source-close whether Datong qishuo 子正/刻 is local apparent solar time, local mean solar time, calibrated clepsydra time, or another conventional coordinate
define the longitude/site to which that historical clock coordinate is attached if source evidence exists
use a modern dynamical ephemeris such as DE431 for Sun/Moon geometry
convert dynamical time to UT with an explicit Delta-T model and uncertainty envelope
apply equation-of-time only if the historically selected clock semantics require apparent solar time
propagate printed-bin and historical-source uncertainty; prefer near-boundary high-information events

next_research_priority.focus: Source-close the absolute time-standard semantics of Datong qishuo 子正/刻: apparent solar, mean solar, clepsydra/conventional, and locality attachment before any ephemeris longitude fit.
